quest.title: Hidden in the Shadows
quest.description: The "Rächer of Solnari" has been revived with the aid of a kuuvahki beam. Now a new crisis looms over Nod-Krai...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1500, Mora x66000, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act III
chapter.title: A Nation That Doesn't Exist

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a few days since we said bye to the others in Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still no news about Rerir, though. Where could he have slunk off to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If only he was gone for good... But with all the trouble he stirred up before, there's no way we've seen the last of him!

dialogues.speaker: Radimir
dialogues.text: Hello! You must be the Traveler and Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Radimir
dialogues.text: Mr. Flins has been looking for you. Unfortunately, there's been a serious Wild Hunt attack over at the quarry. He thinks it's time to regroup and figure out a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt!? Uh-oh, we'd better get over there, right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #C'mon, let's go, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Meet up with Flins at the quarry

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I can barely sense any kuuvahki at all. This whole area feels like a soulless husk.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Looks like his appetite truly is insatiable. As if the power of that Energy Cannon wasn't enough...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: He's not seriously still getting stronger!? What's his endgame here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, everyone's here already. Hey, we made it... So, what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: We've all been on high alert since we split up a few days back, expecting Rerir to strike again.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: But it's like he just vanished into thin air. No one has seen him, nor found any trace of his presence.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: ...That is, until this morning, when a Ratnik found signs of Wild Hunt activity while out here on patrol. As you can see, the Crystonite itself is physically intact, but the kuuvahki it contained is all but completely diminished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And we're sure that Rerir did this?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Who else? He's the only one who could pull off a stunt like this...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Kuuvahki loss has reached critical levels. Rächer of Solnari set to maximum threat level.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Warning: Unless de-escalation measures are taken soon, he will pose a threat beyond our ability to contain. The consequences could be catastrophic.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you remember when we encountered Rerir just after regaining his body?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: There wasn't a shred of sanity left — nothing but madness and rage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Didn't he shout out a bunch of names? Then he started raving about how nothing in this world mattered to him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets chills just thinking about it. But the thought that he's still out there, lurking somewhere in Nod-Krai, waiting for his chance to strike... *shudder* Even chillier.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Last time we fought, we were already at a disadvantage. If he has such overwhelming strength, why would he suddenly go into hiding?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Yeah... If I were him, and I wanted more kuuvahki, I'd just take it by force. No point staying in the shadows.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Unless... something went wrong? His whole resurrection thing didn't exactly go smoothly.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The other thing is... how does someone who's completely lost their mind still have the wherewithal to cover their tracks so perfectly?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Beats me...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: According to certain medical studies, insanity does not always entail a complete loss of rationality. It may be that he is simply living in a world of his own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... actually sounds about right. He was ranting away to himself the whole time, like he had zero interest in talking to us.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: There are many unanswered questions here. He could be right under our noses, and we'd still be in the dark.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Besides his name and title, we know little about him. Certainly nothing about his past or what he might be hoping to achieve.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Exactly — and we wouldn't even know where to begin looking! Even boss hadn't heard of the "Rächer of Solnari" before all this.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: I'd be willing to bet that even if we gathered together every scrap of intel in Nod-Krai, we still wouldn't find more than, like, three useful facts about him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if we do nothing, he'll just keep getting stronger... but if we wanna investigate him, we have no idea where to look.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Last time, we had Marionette and her big robo-buddy to help us, and we still barely held our ground. If we had to face him alone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon's head hurts just thinking about it. What are we supposed to do against a threat this big?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, I do have a little hunch about his next move. Given that he attacked the quarry, I'd say it's likely he'll target other places rich in kuuvahki.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Somewhere like the Eye of Kratti, or the Pillar of Embla. One thing's for sure — if we just sit back and let him keep absorbing kuuvahki, we really won't stand a chance against him.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: A perfectly reasonable hypothesis. However, it is worth noting that these two locations are quite far apart. To investigate them both, we'll need to split up.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I agree, we should split up. Right now, Rerir's goal seems to be gathering kuuvahki, not fighting us directly. Once we're done, let's regroup on Hiisi Island.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...Wait, why Hiisi Island?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: If I recall correctly, your largest goddess statue was carved from kuuvahki-rich ore, was it not?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hmm, that's right... Yes, it could well be a potential target of his. I should head back and start evacuating the pilgrims.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Splitting up's always gonna be risky, but I guess we don't have much choice, right? We're in a race against time here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And if we do run into Rerir... What then?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Heh, that's when you follow the third rule of treasure hunting: Run like the wind!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Didn't you say the third rule was "go with the flow"?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Uhh... I dunno, did I? Anyway, whatever! In this situation, "go with the flow" means "go find backup."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Agreed. If anyone finds so much as a trace of Rerir, do not pursue him. Get out of the area and alert the rest of us as soon as possible. We need to put safety first.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Alright, we'd better get moving. C'mon Ineffa, let's go.

choices.text: He was already extremely dangerous, even then...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Any leads?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Nope, diddly-squat. No clues to where he might be hiding. It's like he's a ghost...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: It feels like we're sitting on a powder keg that could go off at any second... Ugh, I hate this feeling! I'd rather face him head-on than be left hanging like this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you guys didn't find anything either?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: *sigh* Not loving the word "either"... How about you, Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I questioned a few Ratniki and eventually narrowed my investigation down to one suspicious individual. But by the time I got to his place, he was already gone.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Almost as if he knew someone was onto him... Either that, or he's just extremely cautious and doesn't stay in one place for long.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: He's been biding his time for a while now... The question is, where or what is his next target?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: No idea. Since regaining his body, he seems to have lost all interest in the fragment in my possession. If he did still want it, he's had plenty of chances to take it.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: All we can do now is hope that Aino and Ineffa turn up some leads... Darn it, Rerir! If you've got the guts, come face me one-on-one!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...W—Wait, he's actually here!? I didn't mean it, I swear!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: No, it's coming from...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Silvermoon Hall! The Lady Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar might be in danger!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get over there, quick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That was too close...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: We barely made it out of there alive! What's that guy's deal? How'd he get so crazy strong?

choices.text: He's one of the Five Sinners...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: He's a threat to this entire nation. I doubt his strength could even be measured by conventional standards.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: I have a question.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: When me and Ineffa showed up, we saw him chasing after this lady like he wanted her dead. What was that all about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We weren't there for the whole thing either. They were already duking it out by the time we arrived.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Yeah, we didn't see how it all started. It all escalated so quickly, we had no choice but to step in.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar, can you shed any light on the situation?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Kuutar... Cross-checking database... I see. So you're the one that the Frostmoon Scions refer to as the "Moon Goddess"?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: (Wait, she's the Moon Goddess!? Ohhh, no wonder she looks just like all those statues...)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: There are many reasons why people might worship the moon... and just as many why they might despise it.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I've never met that person before, but there was no mistaking his deep-seated hostility towards me.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Why he holds me in such contempt, I cannot say. But since he hunts the power of the moon... it's no surprise that I am a target.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #There are many potential motives. For instance, you helped {NICKNAME} escape his grasp. This could be his way of taking revenge.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: It is also possible that he covets the kuuvahki inside you, and seeks to take it for his own. The list goes on.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But right now, devising a counter-strategy should be our number one priority. The likelihood of this location being discovered is close to 100%.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (A counter-strategy? But we don't stand a chance against an enemy like this...)

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Surely, our only option is to run? He's not gonna chase us to the end of the world, right? So, as long as we can sneak out of Nod-Krai undetected...)

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (...No, I can't say that! Come on, Jahoda, this is serious stuff... You can't suggest we all just chicken out!)

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Running is our only option.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: You seem surprised... But what other choice do we have? We are facing an enemy we cannot possibly defeat in battle.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: W—Well, I mean, yeah... but still...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It's not too late. I can distract him, so you'll have plenty of time to make your escape.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what? You're gonna act as bait!?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Doesn't that make sense? I'm the one he's after. There's no need for you to risk your necks on my behalf.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: A coyote doesn't stop for bypassers while it's howling at the moon.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: What is it, Lauma?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The Frostmoon Scions have already grown accustomed to life without their Goddess. My presence here is no longer essential, and this is not my home, so you needn't ask me to stay.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: We can't just roll over and let him get away with this! That's not our style!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Yeah! We can't just call it quits after everything we've been through together!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (Besides, she pretty much saved my life back there. If I just ditched her now, I'd never forgive myself!)

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We can't overlook that you have saved our lives multiple times now. To talk of returning the favor would be a little crass for my liking, but... suffice to say that we are friends, and friends look out for one another.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Rerir's true objective remains unclear. Even if we were to sacrifice Miss Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar, there's no guarantee he would stop.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But—

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar... I know why you left the Frostmoon Scions so long ago. It was because people started treating prayer as a form of trade.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: They would make self-centered wishes, force you to accept meaningless offerings in return, and then expect you to perform miracles for them as if that were their entitlement.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If it were me, I might have walked away too. But I believe that time can change everything... and that sometimes, it takes losing something precious to appreciate its true worth.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: After much reflection, I've realized that this was never about whether the Frostmoon Scions "need" you.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Any relationship based on need is purely transactional. What I truly hope... is that you'll choose to stay, not out of obligation, but as part of our family.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: You were born here, and now you've returned. Who knows, perhaps it was the moonlight that guided you home.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thank you, Lauma, but my power is on the wane. I'm afraid I will be of little use to you now.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: ...Very well then. I'll do as you say.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Both times you saved us, we were transported across great distances in an instant. Is that one of your powers as the Moon Goddess?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It is, but I find it very draining. I barely managed to pull it off just now... and it will be some time before I'm strong enough to do so again.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Rejected by the world, my power is dwindling — like a lake cut off from its source, slowly shrinking away. Now... it has almost run dry.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: What do you mean, "rejected by the world"?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The three moons belonged to the ancient, bygone era in which they came into being. From the moment I was born, the world itself has been steadily sapping away at my strength.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's why we need the Moon Marrow — to borrow the Eternal Moon's power...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The three moons are not one and the same. As the Goddess of the Frost Moon, I cannot wield the powers of the other two.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Yet moonlight has a way of blending together. Each can reflect the others' glow. So when our fingers touched, I was able to restore my strength by drawing kuuvahki from the Eternal Moon's marrow.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But this method of recovery is painfully slow. If only we could find th—

response.speaker: The Wild Hunt's Roar
response.text: Raargh!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: It's the Wild Hunt!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Ugh, even faster than we expected. We'll have to finish this conversation later.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hmm... See how those Wild Hunt creatures are running away from us? They're likely just a scouting party... Which means, Rerir won't be far behind.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Then what are we waiting for? Let's get the heck outta here!

choices.text: It's our turn to help you now.
We stand and fight, no matter what.
...And that probably wasn't his full strength.

talks.objective: Break out of the Wild Hunt's onslaught

dialogues.text: What's the matter, bit off more than you could chew?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Who the...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Uncle Varka! You're back from Amsvartnir?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you're Varka? Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius!?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We can save the intros for later. Right now, let's get you all out of this hellhole. Follow me — I know somewhere you'll be safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Oh, is that where I think it is?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That's the one. C'mon, move — there's no time to waste!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, where are we? This is so well-hidden...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, well that goes without saying. This is the Knights of Favonius's meeting place in Nod-Krai, and a contact hub for the Northern Intelligence Network.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Northern Intelligence Network...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Aka, the black market of intel. No matter what faction you're with, it's THE place to buy and sell information. Their headquarters are in Nod-Krai, but they've got contacts in every nation.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: As an expeditionary force on foreign soil, working with them has offered us the most effective way of getting our hands on reliable local intel. This is where we meet — so naturally, it's secure.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Anyway, where were we? Folks from Nod-Krai should be pretty familiar with me by now, but I believe this is the first time we've met.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce myself. I am Varka, Knight of Boreas, and Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, we've heard all about you. This meeting's been a long time coming!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You look way younger than Paimon expected! But you definitely have that Grand Master vibe, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, well, I'm no spring chicken. Just not showing my age yet.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Definitely feeling some of that back pain today, though... Rushed back from Amsvartnir without a wink of sleep, only to get right into another fight with that freshly revived maniac...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Another? You mean, you've fought him before?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yep. He wasn't nearly as strong back then, but he was still a formidable foe. I brought some of the Knights along to give him a little "surprise," but he saw us coming from a mile off.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: My squad took heavy injuries, and I barely made it out alive myself. We knew it might have been our last chance, so we staked everything on it... But still, it wasn't enough to stop him.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I tried tracking him down afterwards, but he didn't leave a trace. Even in his unhinged mental state, he's as cautious as any trained operative...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: So I decided to come find you, and as luck would have it, turned up to find you being ambushed by the Wild Hunt. The rest, you already know.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm... Is that why he's been frantically absorbing kuuvahki these past few days? Because he sees you as a threat?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Maybe I'm part of the equation, but even if I weren't, I'm sure he'd still be gathering power. He's clearly working up towards something.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Note to self: Uncle Varka's strength rating officially upgraded.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Guess it's my turn to ask questions now... So, what exactly's been happening in Nod-Krai? Why has the Wild Hunt returned in humanoid form, and why is it after you?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: That's a long story, but I'll try to make it quick...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Aino brings Varka up to speed about what happened before...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Wow, I had no idea so much had happened. Sounds like you guys have really been through it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: So, the Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar is actually a Fatui Harbinger... and all this Wild Hunt activity in Nod-Krai is the work of the "Rächer of Solnari," one of the Five Sinners...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That's a lot to take in. Need some time to wrap my head around it all...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm truly sorry, Mr. Varka.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You stood with us against the Wild Hunt, and did everything you could to stop it from escalating into a full-blown catastrophe. And then, the one time you're away, it all comes to a head and all your hard work gets undone...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You've got nothing to apologize for, Miss Moonchanter.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You can plan a hundred steps ahead and still slip up — that's just life. No one knows what tomorrow holds. You can't predict which way the wind will blow next.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And to be perfectly honest, I can't say I'm surprised. For all the times we've defeated the Wild Hunt in the past, we've never been able to completely wipe it out. Turns out we were just delaying the inevitable.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But now that a new variable has come into play, fate may well take a different course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A new variable? You mean... us?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, who else? And in a strange way, I think his resurgence might not be an entirely bad thing. The Wild Hunt is like an unrelenting force of nature, but Rerir is an individual with an agenda. He's gotta have a weak spot somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That said, while Aino was explaining everything just now, some of the points that Mr. Flins added caught my attention.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You mean about our mystery ally?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That's right. From what you've said, not only did they lead you straight to some key files, they also shielded Hiisi Island from a lethal kuuvahki blast.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I don't know who or what could pull something like that off... Heck, even Miss Columbina doesn't have a clue.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I hadn't heard the story about those files... Would you mind repeating their titles for me?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: "Wild Hunt Phenomena Log," "A Nod-Kraian Ratnik's Field Journal," and "Kuuvahki Survey Log"...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Oh... No, still doesn't ring a bell...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hmm, another dead end... Guess all we can do now is hope that our mystery ally keeps showing up when we most need them.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Still, it's safest to assume they won't be intervening again. From here on out, we'll have to resolve this crisis by ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Your intel also explains something else I've been wondering about. The reason I led my team to Amsvartnir was because we'd had reports about a possible source of the Wild Hunt showing up there.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But once we looked into it, it turned out to be a red herring. I don't know who was behind it, but clearly, it served its purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I doubt it's by chance that he happened to make his comeback while my attention was diverted. And from everything you've told me, it sounds like his scheming began well before his return... so maybe luring me away was all a part of his plan.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (But is it even possible that he orchestrated all of this by himself?)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: (The Moon Maiden and the Rächer of Solnari, in Nod-Krai of all places... The way everything is unfolding, it can't be a coincidence.)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: So... What do we do now? Got any ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Right now, we've got at least three things to consider. Let's go through them one by one.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: First, we need to figure out how to take down Rerir. If we can't beat him in a straight-up fight, the rest won't even matter.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: To my knowledge, the bulk of Nod-Krai's fighting force is already gathered here. But even with everyone united, we're still no match for Rerir in his current state — let alone with his power still growing.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What if there was a way to tap into a new power of our own?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: How so?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you thought of something, Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Three moons once watched over this world: the Eternal Moon was the largest, the Frost Moon was the brightest, and the Iridescent Moon was the most mysterious.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They say that back then, the three Moon Goddesses wielded immense power. Enough to shape the workings of the world itself.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: #I now bear the Frost Moon's power, and the Eternal Moon's marrow resides within {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hold on, are you suggesting...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The Iridescent Moon, the last piece in the puzzle...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That's right. If we can find the Iridescent Moon's marrow, I will be able to regain my strength much more quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The three moons are said to stir the tides and illuminate all things. Perhaps they hold further secrets beyond our understanding.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: According to my analysis, this solution is feasible. However, it is subject to one major condition — how do we locate the Iridescent Moon's marrow?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I know a way, but... We will need to visit the Fatui's Experimental Design Bureau.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Experimental Design Bureau? Are you saying... we need to involve Marionette?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. I must speak with Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It's a long way from here to the Experimental Design Bureau... There's a high chance you'll be spotted. You shouldn't go alone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I will go with her.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Then that's settled. Next up, our second priority — somehow, we need to figure out Rerir's end goal.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: As you saw for yourselves, when he was still in his Wild Hunt form, everything he did was for the sake of recovering his body and resurrecting himself. His first act since then, after laying low for a while, was to try and assassinate this young lady.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: People's obsessions often reveal their greatest vulnerabilities. There must be a reason why he despises the moon so deeply... Perhaps it'd shed some light on his title, the "Rächer of Solnari."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt has plagued Nod-Krai for centuries now. If we want to stop it for good, we have to get to the root cause of what's driving it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It's true... We still know very little about him.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar hadn't given us that lead, we wouldn't even know his name.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: But where would we even start? I doubt even the intel queen of Nod-Krai has a clue, and she has info coming out of her ears...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh? That's a rather hasty conclusion for someone who's so painstakingly meticulous when it comes to dealing with machines.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ah, she heard me...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm now asking myself the same question... I received a letter from a "humble knight of Favonius," requesting a meeting to discuss a major business deal. But it looks like this humble knight had something else in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hahaha, details, details... Miss Nefer, the important thing is that you've arrived at the perfect time.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Since his failed ambush, I've been racking my brains trying to come up with a plan to fight Rerir. Given the severity of the situation, I think it's fair to say that our only chance lies in uniting as one — and I'm talking ALL the factions in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We can't do this without the Curatorium, but I knew it'd be a tough job to win you over. So I took the liberty of reaching out for a little chat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec... How did you even hear about this place, Nefer?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't you say this is meant to be the Knights of Favonius's meeting spot, and a contact hub for the Northern Intelligence Network? And... isn't it supposed to be super hidden?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You really think he could've gotten settled in Nod-Krai without my help? Besides, I'm the one running this gig — of course I know where the meeting place is.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Allow me to introduce the current head of the Northern Intelligence Network. If it's intel you're after, she's your woman. Pretty much seen and heard it all.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Please, spare me the flattery. Let's cut to the chase — seems like you've run into some trouble, huh?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You bring Nefer up to speed on what's been happening...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, this certainly qualifies as an unforeseen crisis. On behalf of the Curatorium of Secrets... I wish you all the best of luck.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: So you're just going to sit this one out?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Why should I get involved? What could possibly be in it for me?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: What if we told you we can't do this without you?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Oh? Then I'd say, you'd better make it worth my while. I don't work for free.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I can't put a price on something like this — it's just not in my nature. But then again, you and I have always been polar opposites in this regard — so I can't exactly say I didn't see this coming.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If you insist on compensation, I will pay you. Consider this a formal commission. Sound fair?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You just don't give up, do you? Heh, too bad — I know you well enough to know you can't afford my prices.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: The riskier the job, the more it'll cost, and a Moonchanter's stipend isn't exactly generous... Unless you're planning to start passing the donation box around among the faithful?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Uhh, boss, just a thought... If they come up short, maybe you can take the difference out of my next few paychecks?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Things got really dangerous during the fight with Rerir. If this girl hadn't saved me, I'd be ley line fodder by now... I'd be gone for good, boss.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: If there's any way we can make this work, I'd really like to help her... Please, I'm begging you!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: This is why I'm always telling you — never accept favors. They're the hardest debts to repay.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You have to be careful who you get involved with, or you invite all kinds of misfortune... *sigh* Very well, Jahoda, I will help — but just this once. Don't count on this happening again.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Flins, that fragment that Rerir was after... Do you still have it on you?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Let me borrow it. I need it to follow up on some leads.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... You actually have some leads!?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Shh... This is top-secret information.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I get it... We all have things we'd rather keep to ourselves. Plus, I know we can count on you, so we'll leave the intel-gathering in your hands.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: And that brings me to the third and final item... We need to find a way to distract him. We need time to make our move, so someone will have to stall him.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'm in for this part, no matter what. Anyone coming with?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Count me in too.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Come off it, you two... Quit playing heroes.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: I'm waaay ahead of you here... Ineffa did a scan of the Moon Goddess's kuuvahki signature, and we're gonna use it to make some decoys over at the Krumkake Craftshop. Anyone who's "in," follow me.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Once they're ready, we'll deploy the decoys across Nod-Krai. So as long as the rest of you keep moving, he won't catch onto your scent and won't be able to track you down.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I like it! Genius idea.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: No biggie!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Alright then, we'll split into three teams.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Once your team has finished their mission, return here and wait for the others. Dismissed!
